subject: Gdistsamp: How to fit a global detection function and estimate density at 42 sites

messages.author: 4951de11d6b58950
messages.subject: Gdistsamp: How to fit a global detection function and estimate density at 42 sites
parts:
Hello,

My apologies if I failed to find a similar archive post.

My study involves one year of bird point count sampling over three repeat visits with distance recorded. I would like to determine density using distance estimation at 42 different sites using a global detection function. The global detection function is necessary, because most of my sites are small fragments where it is impossible to increase sampling intensity.

I selected gdistsamp, because I also wanted to estimate phi and ran the model using site as a covariate with 42 levels. However, the model fails to converge, which doesn't really surprise me given the large number of covariate levels.

Warning message:
In gdistsamp(~site, ~site, ~1, dist.myco1, output = "density"  :
  Hessian is singular. Try using fewer covariates and supplying starting values.

I have tried various models that use starting data from a simpler model and changing K - all fail to converge. Likewise, I've been unable to find a different approach in the archives here or in other published resources.

Many thanks for your help.

Best,
Ian Ausprey

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Gdistsamp: How to fit a global detection function and estimate density at 42 sites
parts:
Estimating a separate density for each site is kind of like estimating a separate intercept for every datum within a standard regression analysis--hence the error. It sounds like maybe you are more interested in the realized density than the expected density? If so, calls to ranef/bup (see ?ranef) after a model has been fit might get you what you need. 

John

Thank you for the advice. This does produce a list of values for realized density, but I don't believe them as they are twice what I get from normal distance estimation and do not reflect the biological reality I know from the field. The other issue is that I would also like to extract estimates of phi per site. But, I appreciate your help.
Ian

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Gdistsamp: How to fit a global detection function and estimate density at 42 sites
parts:
I think you would have to go a Bayesian route to get site-specific phi estimates (lacking any covariates, treating site-specific phi as a random effect). Uncharacteristically high density estimates using gdistsamp has to be one of the most common questions on the board: density in this model relates to lambda(or N) and phi. Consider something like

library(boot)
inv.logit(coef(m1)[2])*bup(ranef(m1))

rather than

bup(ranef(m1))

John

messages.author: 4951de11d6b58950
messages.subject: Re: Gdistsamp: How to fit a global detection function and estimate density at 42 sites
parts:
Thank you again. Your comments have been very helpful in increasing my understanding of this model.

The issue ultimately is that I am trying to combine methods from distance estimation and occupancy modeling to understand how detection probability is governed by two components: (1) how well I am able to detect a vocalizing individual (ie., interspecific variation in effective distance radius) and (2) whether or not a bird is available to detect during a given sampling period (ie., it doesn't vocalization or it's not there).

Hence, the issue with gdistsamp (as I understand it) is that phi is a global estimate while the realized estimates of lambda are site specific. Given that I am predicting that both occupancy and density will vary among my sites due to habitat and landscape differences I ultimately need site-specific densities that reflect site-specific phis. Like I said before the spatial constraints of these sites require a global detection function across sites.

I can get reasonable densities from Distance, but I lose the information afforded by the temporal survey replications.

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Gdistsamp: How to fit a global detection function and estimate density at 42 sites
parts: I confess I don't really understand what you're trying to do (correlate occupancy's p to sigma and phi? develop an integrated model?). You might be able to fit something like gdistsamp(~1, ~site, ~1), but if you are predicting that expected values for occupancy/density vary across sites due to habitat/landscape differences, why not just model lambda and phi as varying this way using covariates rather than as a bunch of different intercepts?

Dear Ian,

this might be a super late answer, but is at the same time linked to a question. I had exactly the same question issue in my abundance analysis. I have also 42 sites and wanted to estimate abundance for each site, but given very low numbers of detections per site per survey, i needed a global estimate of detection probability. At the end I decided to go for programm Distance. I used my predictors of detection probability, which were site specific, to get a global detection probability pooling together the entire dataset. Then,the value of the estimate of global detection probability is entered into the model for density as the only predictor for detection. It worked perfectly.

Now, my question is: did you manage to do this in Unmarked? I am now doing analysis of occupancy in unmarked. And, because of a similar issue like yours, i had decided to separately analyze abundance using the abundance estimates from Distance as response in a normal glm. However, i would still be interested on combinng both in one single model.

Thanks in advance for any update of your question.

Best regards,
Ana.
